name: Webinar Day 0 (Announcement)
description: The first email that introduces the webinar. Sells the PROBLEM, not a deadline -- nobody is waiting for this email yet, unlike a reminder. Pairs with the 'webinar' (reminder) template in this same library: reuse the same registration URL, date and brand across both.
goal: Get the reader to click through to the registration page by making them recognise their own situation, not by pressuring them with urgency -- that is reserved for the reminder emails.
rules: Longer body copy than a reminder is expected: day 0 is where you earn attention, a reminder only has to re-activate it.
Only 2 CTAs, not 3. Pushing hard on a first touch reads as desperate.
No fake scarcity and no 'last chance' language here -- save real urgency for the reminder emails. If you burn it on day 0, the sequence has nowhere left to go.
The two verbatim quotes must be real (sales calls, support tickets, DMs, discovery forms), kept messy and spoken. Invented quotes in clean marketing English are obvious and destroy the effect.
The three CTAs across this and the reminder email all point to the SAME registration URL.
Keep at least 60% real text: an image-heavy email lands in spam and shows up empty when images are blocked.

placeholders.label: Brand name
placeholders.guidance: Used as the logo alt text and in the footer.

placeholders.label: Logo URL
placeholders.guidance: 160-200px wide, transparent PNG, hosted on your own domain.

placeholders.label: Hero visual URL
placeholders.guidance: 600x338 (16:9). On day 0 a face outperforms an abstract graphic: people register for people. A speaker photo or a screen capture of the method works better here than a generic GIF.

placeholders.label: Hero visual alt text
placeholders.example: The speaker presenting the 3-step outreach method

placeholders.label: Hook line (day-0 specific, not used in the reminder)
placeholders.guidance:
Two short lines, 4-9 words each, separated by
. Line 1 is a statement the reader instantly agrees with; line 2 is the twist that opens your topic. Pattern interruption buys the two seconds needed to earn the headline. Formats that work: familiar truth + reversal, insider observation, contradiction. Cultural references land hard here, only if you share that culture with the reader.
placeholders.example:
Everyone wants more leads.
Almost nobody fixes their follow-up first.

placeholders.label: Headline
placeholders.guidance: 6 to 14 words naming the transformation. Day 0 has no deadline to lean on, so the headline carries the value alone. Pick one angle: outcome, gap, or method. Ban 'Join our webinar', 'Newsletter #12', 'Don't miss out'.
placeholders.example: Cold outreach in 2026: what actually gets replies

placeholders.label: Subheadline
placeholders.guidance: One line, 6-14 words: the measurable part the headline couldn't fit.
placeholders.example: The 3-message sequence that books meetings without a bigger list

placeholders.label: Social proof
placeholders.guidance: One real, verifiable number. On day 0 it is your only credibility signal -- the reader has no reason to trust you yet. No number available? Use experience instead, or delete the block. Never invent one.
placeholders.example: 12 years running cold outreach for B2B teams

placeholders.label: Date line above CTA 1
placeholders.guidance: Factual, not pressuring -- day 0 has no real urgency yet.
placeholders.example: 🟢 LIVE WEBINAR | Thursday, 12 March at 10:30 CET

placeholders.label: CTA 1
placeholders.guidance: 2 to 5 words, first person.

placeholders.label: Registration URL
placeholders.guidance: Same URL used in both CTAs here and in the reminder email.

placeholders.label: The situation
placeholders.guidance: One sentence describing the reader's constraint, not the topic. Specificity is what makes it feel personal at scale.
placeholders.example: When you're the only one handling outreach, every reply feels like luck.

placeholders.label: Why now
placeholders.guidance: One sentence on what changed recently and made it worse.
placeholders.example: Especially since inbox filters got stricter in January.

placeholders.label: The problem, named out loud
placeholders.guidance: One sentence, gives the reader permission to be confused. Add an absolving clause -- 'and for good reason', 'it's not their fault'.
placeholders.example: The truth? Most founders are lost on this -- and for good reason.

placeholders.label: Verbatim quote 1 -- the confusion
placeholders.guidance: A REAL quote from a real prospect or customer (sales call, support ticket, DM). Keep the messy, spoken phrasing including hesitations. Do not write it yourself in clean marketing English.

placeholders.label: Verbatim quote 2 -- the paralysis
placeholders.guidance: Same rule as quote 1, about not knowing what to prioritise.

placeholders.label: Immediate cost of inaction
placeholders.example: So you keep sending, with no real way to know what's working.

placeholders.label: Slow cost of inaction
placeholders.example: And the list you should be building keeps getting pushed to next month.

placeholders.label: The pivot
placeholders.guidance: Max 8 words.
placeholders.example: That's exactly what we help you fix.

placeholders.label: Session name
placeholders.guidance: Keep it short and repeat the EXACT same name on the landing page. A mismatch causes drop-off.

placeholders.label: Date, time, timezone
placeholders.guidance: Re-check this every reuse of the template: an inconsistent date destroys credibility.

placeholders.label: Topic line
placeholders.guidance: The transformation, not the subject matter.
placeholders.example: the 3-message sequence that books 8 meetings a week

placeholders.label: Agenda bullet 1
placeholders.guidance: The ingredients of a method that actually works this year.
placeholders.example: Why 80% of outreach sequences get filtered before they're read

placeholders.label: Agenda bullet 2
placeholders.guidance: The speed or effort objection removed.
placeholders.example: How to personalise 50 emails in under an hour, without a VA

placeholders.label: Agenda bullet 3
placeholders.guidance: Your named signature method, most desirable, last.
placeholders.example: The 3-message sequence we use to book 8 meetings a week
